items.title: Mizoram government cannot back out of land sale after regime change in State: Calcutta High Court
items.summary: The Calcutta High Court on Friday ruled that the government of Mizoram could not go back on its agreement to sell a Kolkata property to a private company for approximately ₹38.3 crore, merely because there had been a change in Mizoram's political regime [ State of Mizoram & Others. vs. Excel Vincom Private Limited & Anr ]. A Bench of Justices Arijit Banerjee and Apurba Sinha Ray observed that the decision to backtrack from the sale agreement appeared to be a case of "regime revenge" by the Mizo government that took charge in December 2023. "It does appear to us that this is a case of ‘regime revenge’. The Government cannot renege on a promise made and acted upon by a citizen to his detriment, only because there is a change in regime," the Court said. Finding no justification for cancelling the sale, the Court ordered the government of Mizoram to execute the sale of a plot of land that previously housed a government guesthouse and offices (Mizoram House) within eight weeks. items.title: Stamp duty on arbitral awards must exclude interest component: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently held that stamp duty on an arbitral award must be calculated on the principal amount awarded and not on the interest component even where such interest forms part of the total sum awarded by an arbitral tribunal. [ Patel KNR Infrastructure Ltd v. NHAI ] Justice Jasmeet Singh held that Section 23 of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 makes it clear that the mere inclusion of an interest component in an instrument cannot result in an enhanced stamp duty liability. "The interest component cannot be included in the computation of stamp duty merely because it forms part of the total amount awarded by the Arbitral Tribunal," the Court observed. Justice Jasmeet Singh The Court delivered the ruling while dismissing a review petition filed by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) against an April 2024 order directing it to pay the balance interest due to Patel KNR Infrastructure Limited under an arbitral award.
